task: CPU Socket Coordinate-Mapping Prototype - isolated verification only

step1_visualConfirmation.method: Fresh untitled scene (never saved). Instantiated Motherboard_Quest_Optimized.glb at identity transform (world == raw mesh-local). Placed a red sphere marker as a child at localPosition = rawCoordinate (no offset, no snapping). Rebuilt the 13 material slots on Universal Render Pipeline/Lit preserving each original base color texture (the glTF-pbrMetallicRoughness shader does not render through this project's camera-capture path). Added a temporary camera positioned in the raw -Y region looking toward +Y (the front/populated surface's known outward direction) and a directional light.
step1_visualConfirmation.result: Marker renders centered inside the CPU socket housing cavity on the real baked photographic texture of an MSI B450 TOMAHAWK MAX board, next to the 'CORE BOOST'/'DDR4 BOOST' silkscreen and DIMM slots. A close-up zoom (orthographic size 0.035m) confirms the marker sits inside the flat black socket cavity with a curved retention-lever bracket visible along one edge.

step2_surfaceNormalAndInsertionDirection.method: Pure software ray-triangle intersection (Moller-Trumbore) against Mesh.vertices/GetTriangles() directly, iterating all 12 submeshes. No PhysX Collider or Physics API used (constraint-safe: no collider creation). Ray cast from (rawX, -0.5, rawZ) in direction +Y (from outside the front surface, per the previously-verified finding that raw -Y is the populated/front outward direction), taking the first (nearest) intersection.

independentCoordinateMatch.note: The nearest ray-triangle hit on this XZ column reproduces the stored CPU socket coordinate exactly, independently re-deriving it via raw triangle geometry rather than reusing the stored value directly.

step2_surfaceNormalAndInsertionDirection.cpuSocketPlaneOrientation: Flat, axis-aligned: the socket cavity floor triangle at this point is exactly perpendicular to the mesh's raw Y axis (no tilt/component on X or Z). Normal == board surface normal at this location.
step2_surfaceNormalAndInsertionDirection.insertionDirectionMeaning: The CPU travels opposite to the outward surface normal (i.e. +Y in raw space) to seat into the socket from outside the board's front face toward the socket floor.

step3_pin1Orientation.reason: Angled close-up inspection of the socket cavity (screenshot 04) shows only a flat molded surface with baked-in 'SOCKET AM4' text (confirming socket identity from the real source photograph) and a plain curved retention-lever bracket along one edge. No asymmetric Pin-1 triangle/dot/notch marking is visually discernible at this asset's resolution ('Quest_Optimized' low-poly/simplified geometry). Per instructions, this is reported as Unknown rather than guessed.

step4_candidateCleanReferenceFrame.name: CandidateBoardFrame
step4_candidateCleanReferenceFrame.definition: Temporary GameObject at world identity (position=0, rotation=identity). The model was instantiated as its child with localRotation = Euler(180,0,0) (localPosition=0, localScale=1), so the frame's local axes = raw mesh-local axes rotated 180 degrees about X. This makes the front/populated surface's outward normal point to local/world +Y (up), a more intuitive 'up = front' convention than the raw frame (raw -Y = front).
step4_candidateCleanReferenceFrame.conversionFormula: candidate = R * raw, where R = RotateX(180) = diag(1, -1, -1). Equivalently: candidate.x = raw.x, candidate.y = -raw.y, candidate.z = -raw.z. R is a proper rotation (det = +1, orthonormal) - no shear, no mirroring.
step4_candidateCleanReferenceFrame.insertionDirectionSelfConsistencyCheck: In this frame, +Y is defined as 'up/outward' by construction, and the independently-measured insertion direction converts to exactly -Y ('downward'). This matches ordinary physical intuition (a CPU is lowered down onto its socket) and is an internal consistency signal for the conversion, not additional independent evidence.

step5_conversionVerifiedByRepeatMarker.method: A second, independently-placed marker (cyan) was added as a direct child of CandidateBoardFrame (sibling of the model, NOT nested under it) at localPosition = the CONVERTED coordinate (0.01890, -0.00855, -0.07750), computed fresh from the conversion formula rather than copied from the raw-frame marker's transform. Because CandidateBoardFrame sits at world identity, this local position equals its world position directly.
step5_conversionVerifiedByRepeatMarker.cameraSetup: Top-down orthographic camera at world (0.01890, 0.15, -0.07750) looking straight down (-Y), matching the candidate frame's 'up = front' convention.
step5_conversionVerifiedByRepeatMarker.result: The cyan marker renders centered in the exact same CPU socket cavity as the raw-frame red marker (same board, same silkscreen text visible around it). This confirms the conversion formula round-trips correctly using a genuinely independent placement path (frame-relative coordinate, not a reparented copy of the original marker).

summary.conversionFormula: candidate = (raw.x, -raw.y, -raw.z)  [180 degree rotation about raw mesh-local X axis]
summary.pin1Status: Unknown - no distinguishing visual marking found, not guessed
summary.confidence: High for coordinate mapping, orientation, and insertion direction (two independent re-derivations: software ray-triangle intersection exactly reproduced the stored coordinate with 0.0 diff, and the converted-coordinate marker independently landed on the same visible socket). Unknown/no-confidence for Pin-1 (insufficient asset detail, explicitly not guessed).
